thesis: This episode uses examples like GM and various public companies to illustrate that stock prices can swing significantly due to auction-driven market distortions and overshooting rather than changes in the underlying business. The speaker notes that interest in new public offerings often drives prices up dramatically before fading, suggesting these movements do not necessarily reflect fundamental value.
